messages:
maya: Heads-up — starting the engine rollout (matmul-quant v4) in ~30m across night cohorts. Deploybot staged cohorts 1-4.
maya: Quick note: staging run on a 3090 pool showed thermal throttling + 5–8% tail latency bump after ~45m. Not catastrophic but outside our gating. :warning:
deploy-bot: Deploy job 4872101111 created by maya. cohorts: 1,2,3,4. preflight checks: ok. smoke: ok.
ryan: Can you paste the staging telemetry? want the exact metric.
maya: paste below (truncated):
```
gpu_thermal: 83->92C  (3090-x)
latency_p95: 142ms -> 155ms
kv_miss_rate: 0.8% -> 1.1%
error_rate: 0.01% -> 0.02%
```
maya: This is reproducible on our smaller perf runs. NV power capping looks normal.
sarah: Hmm — that temp looks high but borderline. Is quant kernel switching at long sequences? could be matmul path fallback.
maya: Yes, long sequences trigger a different matmul kernel. The new kernel is faster normally but may use more SMs briefly.
ops-oncall: Do we have a rollback safe path? if we hold, what's impact to customers?
ryan: My vote: hold the rollout for cohorts 2-4, let cohort 1 run at 10% traffic for another 30m while we dig in. If cohort1 stays stable, we proceed. If it degrades further, pin back to runtime@v3.9 for all cohorts and abort.
sarah: Agreed. Also create an immediate canary that forces older matmul kernel on 3090 hostgroup to validate.
maya: done: /deploy add-canary --hosts 3090-night --force-kernel matmul-v3 --ttl 1h
maya: Also opening a quick changelog entry for release-notes: add "experimental matmul-v4; thermal profile observed in some 3090s; opt-in via runtime flag"
ryan: ops-oncall — can you update the incident chat channel if cohort1 shows >10% p95 increase? we should be ready to revert quickly.
ops-oncall: will monitor. set alert p95_increase_threshold=10% for rollout job 4872101111.
deploy-bot: cohorts 2,3,4 have been PAUSED by admin hold. cohort1 continues at 10% traffic.
maya: Running a quick perf diff to compare matmul-v3 vs v4 across sequence lengths 64/256/1024. ETA 25m.
sarah: If we end up pinning, let's ensure release notes clearly state the pin and why, and add a follow-up issue to re-evaluate after thermal kernel telemetry improvement.
ryan: If we pin, command is: `/deploy pin runtime@v3.9 --scope=night-rollout --reason="thermal spike on 3090 with matmul-v4"`
maya: perf diff complete — short seq (64): v4 wins 6% p50, medium (256): even, long (1024): v4 regress 7% p95 on 3090s. I think kernel heuristic misfires on long sequences.
ryan: OK that's our signal. I'm authorizing a pin. maya, can you run the pin and create the rollback PR for release notes?
maya: Pinning now. `/deploy pin runtime@v3.9 --scope=night-rollout --reason="thermal spike on 3090 with matmul-v4"`
deploy-bot: runtime pinned to v3.9 for scope night-rollout by maya. auto-unpin after 72h unless removed.
maya: Created PR #4927: "Pin runtime to v3.9 for night rollout — thermal regression on matmul-v4" including telemetry and perf diffs.
sarah: Added issue #4928 to re-evaluate matmul kernel heuristic and add host-level power telemetry.
ops-oncall: Monitoring — cohort1 metrics trending back to baseline after pin. will call if anything else flares.
ryan: Good catch — thank you. After morning sync we can schedule a deeper stress run on 3090 fleet and a targeted kernel revert test.
maya: note for release notes: "Rollout of matmul-quant v4 paused and runtime pinned to v3.9 due to thermal regressions on some 3090 hosts; investigation ongoing; follow-up issue #4928."
ryan: Thanks team. I'll close this thread after we confirm the morning stress runs. :thumbsup:
